title: Logic Chain — PhD Thesis Butler v4.0
description: Describes a complete INTRO→CONCLUSION logic chain: ordered stages from introduction through conclusion, with required subtypes, template counts, and completeness scoring.

chain_id.description: Unique logic chain ID following convention: chain_{incremental_id}

discipline.description: Academic discipline this logic chain is associated with.

stage_name.description: Descriptive name of the stage (e.g., 'Обоснование проблемы', 'Формулировка гипотезы').

category.description: DIS category this stage maps to.

required_subtypes.description: Required rhetorical subtypes or AREF categories that must appear at this stage (e.g., 'АКТУАЛЬНОСТЬ', 'ЦЕЛЬ_ЗАДАЧИ', 'обзор_литературы').

min_templates.description: Minimum number of templates expected at this stage for a complete chain.

typical_transition_to_next.description: Russian phrase or pattern that typically transitions from this stage to the next.
examples: На основе проведённого обзора сформулированы задачи исследования
Полученные результаты позволяют перейти к экспериментальной проверке

stages.description: Ordered array of stages from INTRO through CONCLUSION. Each stage represents a logical step in the dissertation's argumentation chain.

chain_completeness_score.description: Completeness score (0.0–1.0). 1.0 = all stages present with required subtypes and min_templates met. Weighted by stage importance.

gap_category.description: If completeness_score < 1.0, identifies the DIS category where the primary gap exists. Null if chain is complete.

evidence_count.description: Evidence metadata for this logic chain record.

count.description: Number of source papers exhibiting this logic chain pattern.

source.description: Source identifier. For private builds: paper_id(s). For public output: 'abstracted'.

confidence.description: Confidence: high (≥30 papers), medium (10-29), low (<10), pending (not computed).

source.description: Origin institution or collection. For public output: 'abstracted'.
